contexts.context_excerpt: Course Delivery Methods Overview Metro State offers courses in several delivery formats. Students should review the delivery method before registering to ensure the format fits their schedule and learning preferences. In-Person Courses meet on campus at scheduled days and times. Attendance is required. Online Asynchronous Coursework is completed online without scheduled meeting times. Students work independently but must meet deadlines. Online Synchronous Courses meet online at scheduled times using video conferencing. Attendance is required during meeting times. Hybrid Courses combine in-person meetings with online coursework. The schedule specifies which sessions are on campus and which are online. HyFlex Students may choose to attend each class session in person, online synchronously, o

Financial Aid Overview Metro State offers several types of financial support to help students pay for their education. The university emphasizes affordability and provides guidance throughout the financial aid application process. Types of Financial Aid - Loans: Borrowed funds that must be repaid after graduation or when enrollment drops below half-time. - Grants: Need-based aid that does not need to be repaid. - Scholarships: Merit-based or need-based awards that do not require repayment. - Student Jobs: On-campus or approved off-campus employment opportunities that help students earn money to support educational expenses. Support for Students Metro State assists students with: - Understanding financial aid options - Completing the financial aid application process - Identifying available

Fees Overview Metro State charges several fees in addition to tuition. These fees apply to all courses taken for credit, including online courses. All fees are subject to change. Per-Credit Fees - Activity Fee: $4 per credit. - Student Center Fee: $8.50 per credit. Supports the construction, maintenance, and operation of the student center. - Technology Fee: $14 per credit. Supports student computer labs and instructional technology. - MSUSA Fee: $0.80 per credit. Supports statewide student representation and activities. - Healthcare Fee: $2 per credit. Helps provide access to contracted health services. - Parking Fee: $13 per credit. Supports construction, maintenance, and operation of campus parking facilities. Other Fees - Graduate application fee: $20 - Doctoral application fee: $40 -

responses.answer_text: Financial aid is applied to student accounts to cover tuition, fees, and other university charges after enrollment is verified and eligibility requirements are met. Any remaining funds are refunded to the student through the university’s refund process.

contexts.context_excerpt: Financial Aid Disbursement Overview Financial aid is applied to student accounts after enrollment is verified and eligibility requirements are met. Disbursement typically occurs after the start of the term. How disbursement works: - Aid is first applied to tuition, fees, and other university charges - Any remaining funds are refunded to the student - Disbursement timing varies by term - Students must maintain eligibility and meet enrollment requirements Refunds are issued through the university’s refund process once aid has been applied.

Return to Title IV (R2T4) Overview Federal regulations require the university to review financial aid eligibility when a student withdraws before completing more than 60 percent of a term. This process determines how much federal aid the student earned. Key points: - Applies when a student withdraws from all courses - Aid is prorated based on the percentage of the term completed - Unearned aid must be returned to the federal government - Students may owe a balance to the university after the calculation - The policy applies only to federal financial aid programs Students considering withdrawal are encouraged to consult financial aid staff.

Financial Aid Overview Metro State offers several types of financial support to help students pay for their education. The university emphasizes affordability and provides guidance throughout the financial aid application process. Types of Financial Aid - Loans: Borrowed funds that must be repaid after graduation or when enrollment drops below half-time. - Grants: Need-based aid that does not need to be repaid. - Scholarships: Merit-based or need-based awards that do not require repayment. - Student Jobs: On-campus or approved off-campus employment opportunities that help students earn money to support educational expenses.
